findings.title: slice(1, limit + 1) drops the first (newest) row of every page
findings.explanation: The page is built with rows.slice(1, limit + 1), which skips index 0. Every page loses its first invoice, and each page returns only limit - 1 items when there are more rows. Since next_before is the last id of the page and the next page starts with id < that, the skipped invoice is never returned on any page. This is silent data loss in a financial listing. Use rows.slice(0, limit).

findings.title: next_before can throw or be wrong when page is empty or mis-sliced
findings.explanation: page[page.length - 1].id is dereferenced when hasMore is true. With the current slice(1, ...) and limit = 1, rows has 2 items, hasMore is true, and page has 1 item, so it works only by accident. With limit = 0 (if it is allowed), rows.length > 0 is true and page is empty, so page[-1] is undefined and the handler throws a TypeError, returning a 500. Fix the slice and make sure limit is validated to be >= 1.

findings.title: Validate and cap limit
findings.explanation: The diff does not show how limit is parsed. limit + 1 is now sent to the DB, so if limit comes from the query string as a string, limit + 1 becomes string concatenation (e.g. '10' + 1 = '101'), which would fetch 101 rows and break hasMore. Confirm limit is coerced to a number, is an integer >= 1, and has an upper bound so clients cannot request huge pages. Same applies to before being validated as a bigint.

findings.title: No tests for the pagination boundaries
findings.explanation: This change is about boundary conditions, and the bug in the slice would have been caught by a simple test. Add tests for: fewer than limit rows, exactly limit rows (next_before null), limit + 1 rows (next_before set and the full page returned with no missing items), and an empty result. Also check that paging through all pages returns every invoice exactly once.

findings.title: Clarify naming
findings.explanation: Consider naming the variables something like pageRows/hasNextPage, and add a short comment explaining the limit + 1 lookahead so future readers do not remove it as an off-by-one.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Fix next_before when the last page is exactly full

When the last page had exactly `limit` invoices, `next_before` was still set, so the web app made one extra request that came back empty. This fetches `limit + 1` rows to know whether another page exists.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts
index b9edb19..8e99e4e 100644
--- a/src/routes/invoices.ts
+++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts
@@ -19,11 +19,13 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/', async (req, res) => {
       WHERE org_id = $1 AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR id < $2)
       ORDER BY id DESC
       LIMIT $3`,
-    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit],
+    [req.user.orgId, before ?? null, limit + 1],
   )
+  const hasMore = rows.length > limit
+  const page = rows.slice(1, limit + 1)
   res.json({
-    invoices: rows.map(serializeInvoice),
-    next_before: rows.length === limit ? rows[rows.length - 1].id : null,
+    invoices: page.map(serializeInvoice),
+    next_before: hasMore ? page[page.length - 1].id : null,
   })
 })
```
